questions.question: Who among the following scientists is known for his contribution in the field of genetics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gregor Johann Mendel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor Johann Mendel** is regarded as the **Father of Genetics**.
 
• He conducted experiments on **pea plants (Pisum sativum)** to understand the principles of inheritance.
 
• His work led to the formulation of the **three laws of inheritance**: the Law of Segregation, the Law of Independent Assortment, and the Law of Dominance.
 
• He introduced the concept of **dominant and recessive traits**, which are fundamental in understanding genetic traits.
 
• Mendel’s research was published in 1866 but gained recognition only in the early 20th century when his work was rediscovered.
 
• He laid the foundation for the study of **heredity and genetic variation**, which are crucial in fields like biotechnology, agriculture, and medicine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Michael Faraday**__
 __
 
• **Michael Faraday** was a British scientist known for his contributions to the fields of **electromagnetism and electrochemistry**.
 
• He discovered the principles of **electromagnetic induction, diamagnetism, and electrolysis**.
 
• Faraday’s work laid the foundation for the development of modern electrical technologies, including the **electric motor and transformer**.
 
 
 
• **James Clerk Maxwell**__
 __
 
• **James Clerk Maxwell** was a Scottish scientist best known for his formulation of **Maxwell’s equations**, which describe the behavior of **electric and magnetic fields**.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for **modern physics** and the development of **electromagnetic theory**.
 
• He also made significant contributions to the study of **thermodynamics and the kinetic theory of gases**.
 
 
 
• **JJ Thomson**__
 
 
• **JJ Thomson** was an English physicist credited with the discovery of the **electron** in 1897.
 
• He proposed the **plum pudding model** of the atom, which described the atom as a sphere of positive charge with negatively charged electrons embedded within it.
 
• Thomson was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in 1906 for his work on the conduction of electricity in gases.

• A reduction in the leverage ratio as per **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** norms implies that banks are allowed to maintain a lower proportion of capital relative to their assets.
 
• This means banks can provide **more loans** or increase lending activities while maintaining the **same capital base**, as the regulatory requirement for capital adequacy has been relaxed.
 
• Such measures can stimulate economic growth by enhancing the availability of credit in the market.
 
• It is particularly beneficial in situations where there is a need to boost investment and consumption in the economy.

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because a cut in the leverage ratio does not restrict lending. Instead, it allows banks to lend more with the same capital base.
 
 
 
• **equally, growing**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the leverage ratio does not directly relate to equal lending or a growing capital base; it focuses on the proportion of capital to assets.
 
 
 
• **more, falling**__

questions.question: Stagflation is a typical combination of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Avaruddh Vikas aur Badhtee hui Mudrasphiti (Stagflation)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stagflation**, or मुद्रास्फीति जनित मंदी, refers to a combination of **economic stagnation** (low or negative growth) and **high inflation rates**.
 
• It is characterized by a situation where the **economy does not grow**, unemployment remains high, and inflation continues to rise.
 
• Unlike regular economic slowdowns or recessions, stagflation is unique because **inflation persists** despite a lack of growth.
 
• This phenomenon challenges traditional economic theories which suggest that inflation and economic stagnation rarely occur simultaneously.
 
• It is often caused by **supply shocks** (e.g., increased oil prices) or poor economic policies like excessive money supply or inefficient governance.
 
• The term stagflation gained prominence during the **1970s oil crisis**, where Western economies experienced high inflation and slow growth simultaneously.
 
• Stagflation is considered particularly challenging for policymakers because measures to reduce inflation (e.g., tightening monetary policy) can further slow down economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Avaruddh Vikas aur Girtee hui Mudrasphiti**__

 __
 
• This situation represents economic stagnation combined with **deflation**, where prices are falling rather than rising.
 
• Deflation can be harmful to the economy as it discourages spending and investment, leading to further economic slowdown.
 
• It is more common during severe recessions or depressions, such as during the **Great Depression of the 1930s**.
 
 
 
• **Avaruddh Utpadakta parantu Sthir Mudrasphiti**__
 __
 
• This represents a scenario where **productivity stagnates** but inflation rates remain stable.
 
• While not ideal, stable inflation is generally considered better than high inflation or deflation.
 
 
 
• **Avaruddh Utpadakta aur Badhtee hui Mudrasphiti**__
 
 
• This is similar to stagflation but primarily highlights a lack of **productivity growth** rather than the broader economic stagnation.
 
• It focuses on challenges related to supply-side inefficiencies, such as poor infrastructure or labor market issues.

questions.question: The words 'Do-Aspa' and 'Sinha-Aspa' are related to the which settlement?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Manasabdari**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The terms **'Do-Aspa'** and **'Sih-Aspa'** are related to the **Manasabdari system**.
 
• The **Manasabdari system** was introduced by **Akbar**, one of the greatest Mughal emperors, as an administrative and military system.
 
• In this system, officials and nobles were assigned a **rank (Mansab)**, which determined their position and salary in the administration.
 
• The rank was expressed in terms of two numbers: **Zat** (personal rank) and **Sawar** (cavalry rank).
 
• The terms **'Do-Aspa'** and **'Sih-Aspa'** were related to the cavalry rank (**Sawar**) and represented the number of horses a Mansabdar was required to maintain.
 
• These terms indicated **higher ranks**, where 'Do-Aspa' required two horses and 'Sih-Aspa' required three horses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iqta System**__

 __
 
• The **Iqta system** was introduced by the **Delhi Sultanate** and further developed by rulers like **Iqta**.
 
• Under this system, land was assigned to nobles or officers in place of salary.
 
• The holders of Iqtas, called **Iqtadars** or **Muqtis**, were responsible for collecting revenue and maintaining law and order in their regions.
 
 
 
• **Dahsal System**__
 __
 
• It was introduced during the reign of **Akbar** as a revenue settlement system.
 
• Under this system, the average revenue of the last **ten years** (Dahsala) was calculated to determine the state's share of agricultural produce.
 
• This system formed the basis for **land revenue collection** during Akbar's reign.
 
 
 
• **Mahalwari System**__
 
 
• The Mahalwari system was introduced by the British in India.
 
• Under this system, **land revenue** was assessed based on the entire village or Mahal.
 
• It was implemented in regions like **Punjab, North-West Province, and parts of Central India**.
 
• The responsibility of revenue collection was given to the village community or landlords.

questions.question: In the context of fiscal policy of the Indian economy, which of the following is obtained by subtracting inputs from economic output?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**GVA (Gross Value Added)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GVA (Gross Value Added)** is a measure of the value of goods and services produced in an area, industry, or sector of an economy.
 
• It is calculated by deducting the value of intermediate consumption (inputs) from the total output.
 
• **GVA** provides a sector-wise breakdown of an economy, helping in identifying the contributions of each sector to the overall GDP.
 
• It serves as a key indicator for measuring the economic health of a country or region.
 
• The formula for calculating GVA is: **GVA = Output - Intermediate Consumption**.
 
• In India, the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO) calculates **GVA** at both basic prices and factor cost.
 
• **GVA** is essential for determining the Gross Domestic Product (GDP), as GDP is derived by adding taxes and subtracting subsidies from GVA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NVA (Net Value Added)**__

 __
 
• **NVA** is calculated by deducting depreciation from **Gross Value Added (GVA).**
 
• It provides a more accurate measure of the value generated as it accounts for the wear and tear of fixed assets.
 
• The formula for NVA is: **NVA = GVA - Depreciation.**
 
 
 
• **GDP (Gross Domestic Product)**__
 __
 
• **GDP** represents the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.
 
• It is derived by adding net taxes (taxes minus subsidies) to **Gross Value Added (GVA).**
 
• GDP is a key indicator used to gauge the economic health of a country.
 
 
 
• **SNA (System of National Accounts)**__
 
 
• **SNA** is an international framework for compiling national accounts, established by the **United Nations, International Monetary Fund, World Bank, and other organizations.**
 
• It provides detailed and comprehensive guidelines for calculating economic indicators such as GDP, GVA, and NVA.
 
• The SNA ensures consistency in economic statistics across countries.

questions.question: Total factor productivity is the _______ of the weighted average of output and inputs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Total Factor Productivity (TFP)** is defined as the **ratio** of the weighted average of output to the weighted average of inputs.
 
• It measures the **efficiency** with which inputs like labor and capital are used to produce outputs in an economy.
 
• TFP is considered a key indicator of **technological advancement** and plays a crucial role in determining the growth of an economy.
 
• It accounts for the portion of output growth that cannot be explained by the increase in input usage, often attributed to factors like **innovation, skill improvement, and better resource allocation.**
 
• It helps identify whether an economy or a business is improving productivity through better techniques and innovation rather than simply increasing inputs.
 
• TFP is critical for analyzing the long-term growth potential of an economy and is often used in the study of **economic development and growth models.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Product**__
 __
 
• The term "product" refers to the **result of multiplying two or more values.**
 
• In the context of productivity, "product" does not fit as TFP is not the multiplication of outputs and inputs but rather their ratio.
 
 
 
• **Difference**__
 __
 
• The "difference" refers to the **subtraction** of one quantity from another.
 
• In TFP, outputs and inputs are not subtracted but compared as a ratio to evaluate productivity.
 
 
 
• **Sum**__
 
 
• "Sum" implies the **addition of two or more values.**
 
• However, in TFP calculations, the focus is on the proportional relationship (ratio) between outputs and inputs, not their summation.
 
 
</ul
